findings.finding: Complete two-page score confirms four cellos; no scoring mismatch.

grade.basis: Both score pages inspected. Extremely slow sustained upper-register first-cello line, with exposed tuning and controlled long bows rather than velocity. About level 4 individual demand, plus one for sustaining the quartet sonority; the unusually spare texture does not make this an elementary cello part.

findings.finding: Complete 21-page score confirms three violins; instructional title does not imply beginner difficulty.

grade.basis: Score pp.1,10,21 sampled across the set: Allegro eighth-note imitation, chromatic thirty-second-note runs and trills in the Nocturne, and light articulated closing gestures. First violin has the highest and most exposed line, though activity circulates. Advanced control and shifting; ensemble adds no separate level.

findings.finding: Complete score explicitly says four talking violists; supplied instrumentation correctly includes speaking.

grade.basis: Manuscript score pp.1,7,14 sampled. Players speak Shakespeare while alternating arco/pizzicato material, chromatic figures, tremolo/trill textures and differing tuplets. Individual demand approximately level 6, raised one for independent rhythmic and spoken coordination. Hardest-part choice is approximate because roles circulate.

findings.finding: Three-violin score explicitly offers viola as an alternative third part. Three violins is a valid scoring, not a mismatch.

grade.basis: Score PDF pp.2,3,4,6 sampled, including opening Andante, Allegretto, Adagio and final pages of the suite (scan has imposed non-sequential printed pages). First violin carries higher lyrical lines and chromatic runs; lower parts also have quick ornamental figures. Advanced rather than diploma-level writing, without a full ensemble uplift.

findings.finding: Complete score confirms three violins, C minor, Allegro moderato; no scoring mismatch.

grade.basis: Score PDF pp.2,4,6 sampled. First violin repeatedly climbs into the upper register in slurred chromatic lines, with ornaments and triplets; lower parts use substantially simpler accompaniment and occasional imitative entries. Level 5 reflects the recurring first-part position work and polished articulation, without additional ensemble uplift.

findings.finding: Complete score confirms four violins, including low fourth-violin foundation, not a viola or cello substitution.

grade.basis: Score pp.2,5,9,11 sampled across all three movements. Expressive upper first violin and closing continuous sixteenth-note figures contrast with Gavotta; second violin has repeated double stops. Whole-work demand sits at advanced level, without a separate ensemble uplift; the writing remains idiomatic and tonally clear.

findings.finding: Complete eight-page score is the original three-violin version; other arrangements in the raw source were not used.

grade.basis: Score pp.1,4,8 sampled. Lively quarter=170 repeated eighths include sul-G articulation; first violin later sustains exceptionally high notes through the upper ledger lines, while lower players keep the pulse and double-stop ostinati. Pre-diploma whole-work demand, driven by upper-register security and repeated bow control, with no additional uplift.

findings.finding: PDF supplies complete score and parts for three cellos; no scoring mismatch.

grade.basis: Score pp.1,5 and third-cello part p.11 sampled. Furioso eighth=144 writing places recurring first-cello figures well above the bass staff, with flats/naturals, shifting and accented/slurred pairs; 7/8 and 6/8 transitions and pizzicato exchanges require attention. Level 6 from the sustained upper-register cello task, without an additional ensemble uplift.

findings.finding: Publisher confirms 2002 original for twelve violas, 14 minutes. The composer note identifies first viola as leader of the high cantilena. Later orchestral-version wording elsewhere on the same page must not be imported into this scoring.

grade.basis: Composer programme note for the original twelve-viola work gives specific technical evidence: rosinless bows and near-silent rapid activity, a high first-viola cantilena, then aggressive fast music with fully rosined bows. Professional level 8 is a calibrated inference from those demands and twelve independent voices, including at most one ensemble uplift from level 7. No score inspected; exact ranges and fingerings are unverified.

findings.finding: IRCAM and the composer-hosted catalogue confirm twelve cellos, 1976, approximately eight minutes; no electronics or extra player appears in the stated formation. Supplied analytical material gives work-specific spatial and opening-texture evidence, but is not a playable score.
IRCAM confirms formation, duration and Berlin Philharmonic performers.
Cached analytical PDF, printed pp.44 and 63, describes circular placement and the opening rotation around three pitches; it does not rank numbered cello parts.

grade.basis: Evidence-based estimate, not a score reading: the supplied analytical PDF (printed pp.44,63) identifies circular placement and a rotating opening around three pitches, with displaced melodic lines forming a sound halo. That requires independent pulse, precise distributed attacks and collective control of a homogeneous twelve-cello texture. Professional level 8 represents approximately level 7 individual demand plus one for ensemble coordination. The evidence does not distinguish a uniquely hardest numbered part: cello1 is a representative assignment and the least secure field. No claim is made about exact ranges, double stops or specific bar-level techniques.
